name: San Francisco
useRecordName: Certificate of Occupancy (the permitted use on file with DBI)
disclaimer: Demo-grade, simplified rules. Not legal advice. Always confirm with the responsible department.
examples: Open a 20-seat café with a small kitchen in a ground-floor storefront in the Mission
Add a rooftop deck to my house in the Sunset
Run English tutoring classes for 10 kids from my home in Richmond District
Put up an illuminated sign above my shop on Valencia Street

permits.name: Business Registration Certificate
permits.agency: Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector
permits.appliesWhen: Doing any business in San Francisco, including home-based businesses.

permits.name: Change of use (Planning approval)
permits.appliesWhen: Changing a space's use, e.g. retail to restaurant, or residential to commercial. Some districts require neighborhood notice or a Conditional Use hearing.

permits.name: Building permit (alterations)
permits.appliesWhen: Structural work, new walls, plumbing, electrical, kitchens, decks or rooftop additions.
documents: Plans by a licensed architect or engineer

permits.name: Health permit to operate (food facility)
permits.agency: Department of Public Health, Environmental Health
permits.appliesWhen: Preparing, selling or serving food or drinks to the public. Requires plan check before construction.
documents: Food facility plans and equipment list

permits.name: Fire plan review and Place of Assembly permit
permits.appliesWhen: Commercial kitchens with hoods, renovations reviewed by DBI, or spaces where 50+ people gather.

permits.name: Sign permit
permits.agency: Department of Building Inspection (DBI) with Planning review
permits.appliesWhen: Installing or changing a business sign, especially illuminated or projecting signs.
documents: Sign drawings with size, location and lighting

permits.name: Home-based business (home occupation) rules
permits.appliesWhen: Running a business from your home. Limits apply to floor area, visitors, employees and signage.
documents: Description of activity, hours and expected visitors

zoningNotes: Residential districts (RH-1, RH-2) prohibit most commercial uses; a café or classroom there is usually not allowed.
Neighborhood Commercial (NC) districts allow restaurants, but a change of use can trigger 30-day neighborhood notification (Section 311) or a Conditional Use hearing.
Formula retail (11+ locations worldwide) needs Conditional Use authorization in most NC districts.
Rooftop decks and additions need a building permit and may need neighborhood notification; unpermitted work must be legalized before a sale.
Home-based businesses cannot have frequent client visits, outside employees or exterior signs beyond small limits.
